hints: Focus on what litmus tells you, whether each solution formed is acidic, alkaline or neutral.
Remember that oxides of metals like Na and Ca give alkaline solutions, while their chlorides usually just dissolve to give neutral solutions.
Think about which element forms both an acidic oxide and a chloride that hydrolyses in water to give acid, so both turn blue litmus red.
walkthrough:
**Understand the litmus test**

Think of litmus as a simple acid or alkali detector. Blue litmus turns red in acid, red litmus turns blue in alkali. For the two solutions to have the same effect, both must be acidic, both alkaline, or both neutral.

**Check metal oxides vs metal chlorides**

Metal oxides are basic. For example:
$$\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{NaOH}$$
$$\text{CaO} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2$$
These turn red litmus blue. But their chlorides, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CaCl}_2$, just dissolve without hydrolysis to give neutral solutions with no effect on litmus. So they do not match.

**Check aluminium**

Aluminium oxide, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, is insoluble in water, so it has no effect on litmus. Aluminium chloride hydrolyses strongly:
$$[\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Al}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{OH})]^{2+} + \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$$
This gives an acidic solution. No effect versus acidic is not the same, so this fails too.

**Check phosphorus**

Phosphorus(V) oxide is strongly acidic:
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$$
Phosphorus(V) chloride also hydrolyses completely to give acids:
$$\text{PCl}_5 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 5\text{HCl}$$
Both solutions are acidic and both turn blue litmus red. This is the match we need.

options.A: Aluminium oxide is insoluble and has no effect on litmus, while aluminium chloride hydrolyses to give an acidic solution containing $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$. The effects are different, so this is incorrect.
options.B: Calcium oxide gives alkaline $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ which turns red litmus blue, but calcium chloride dissolves to give a neutral solution with no litmus change. The common trap is forgetting that Group 2 chlorides do not hydrolyse.
options.C: Sodium oxide gives strongly alkaline $\text{NaOH}$ which turns red litmus blue, but sodium chloride gives a neutral solution. Different effects, so this is incorrect.
options.D: Both phosphorus oxide and phosphorus chloride give acidic solutions. $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ forms phosphoric acid and $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolyses to phosphoric acid plus $\text{HCl}$. Both turn blue litmus red, so the effects match.
